name: Bali (Nigeria)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Bibaali (Nigeria): only Bennett 1983 / Boyd & Pasch 1988 classification refs and Blench comments; no description covering stress found

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page bali1245 (refs: Bennett 1983; Boyd & Pasch 1988; Blench n.d; Campbell et al. 2022) and AdaGram (LLACAN) talks/publications pages; Mainz Adamawa Languages Project pages
sources.note: Bibliographic/portal pages only; no Bali/Maya description beyond those listed; AdaGram covers Kugama and Nyesam only; Mainz site has no Yandang-group subpage.

sources.citation: Zheltov, A. Ju. 2014. Peterburgskaja lingvisticheskaja ekspedicija v Nigeriju. Vestnik SPbGU ser. 13, 2014(3): 152-154.
sources.note: Expedition report: Maya worked on by Zheltov (2012-2014), Wakka by Lyakhovich, Yendang by Anikina, Kugama by Litvinova; 'phonology, tonology and morphosyntax' collected; no linguistic statements.

sources.citation: Zheltov, Alexander. 2022. Towards the phenomenon of morphemic and submorphemic neutralization: the case of personal pronouns in some Adamawa languages. Language in Africa 3(2): 259-271. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2022-3-2-259-271
sources.note: Maya (Bali) pronoun paradigms with tone marks; 'tone is unmarked if it is still unclear'; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Zheltov, Alexander. 2020. Plurality marking in Leko and Yendang groups (Adamawa, Niger-Congo) with some reference to noun classification. Language in Africa 1(3): 125-154. doi:10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-125-154
sources.note: Sec. 2 'Data' (p. 128-129): Maya (bcn) data from Yola field trips 2012-2014, 'very preliminary.. still more phonetic than phonological, the tonal notation needs to be specified'; fn. 8 and fn. 20: the only other Maya sources are 'A Guide.. 2007' (orthography-workshop brochure) and Blench 2009 wordlist. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Zheltov, A. Ju. 2016. Elementy morfosintaksisa jazyka maja (adamaua, niger-kongo). In: Vinogradov, V. A. et al. (eds.), Issledovanija po jazykam Afriki 6, 81-89. Moscow: Kljuch-S / Institut jazykoznanija RAN. (open PDF of the whole volume at iling-ran.ru/library/africa/)
sources.note: pp. 81-82: one paragraph on phonology: 'phonology and tonology of Maya require further study; 3 register tones can be stated with confidence; contour tones appear in some contexts, phonological status open; implosives b, d and a final glottal stop'. Nothing on stress or accent. Only first-hand description of Maya = Bali (bcn); rest of article is number, attributives, pronoun paradigms.

sources.citation: Zheltov, A. Ju. 2013. Materialy k sravnitel'nomu izucheniju jazykov adamaua: stoslovniki i sistemy mestoimenij. In: Afrikanskij sbornik 2013, 307-322. St Petersburg: MAE RAN.
sources.note: 100-word lists and pronoun/fusion tables incl. 'maja (bali)'; warns that phonetic transcription and tonal notation are preliminary; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger (analysis); Kato, Barau & Yoder, Zachariah (wordlists). n.d. [c. 2009]. The Maya [Yendang] languages: wordlists collected by Barau Kato and Zachariah Yoder. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation. 15 pp. (Glottolog ref 158487; Internet Archive copy of rogerblench.info. group/Comparatie)
sources.note: Tone-marked comparative wordlist (Bali, Kpasham, Yoti, Yandang) with etymological commentary; introduction says 'little has been published on these languages'; no prose on tone or stress.
Stub: names (Bibaali, Maya, Ibaali), classification, speaker numbers; no phonology.

sources.citation: Zheltov, Alexander. Any post-2016 fuller write-up of Maya (Bali) phonology/tonology from the St Petersburg Adamawa expeditions (announced as 'requiring further study' in 2016; field data 2012-2014).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Zheltov is the only linguist with first-hand Maya data; a phonology chapter, if written, would be the place a stress/accent statement appears.

sources.citation: Kato, Barau & Yoder, Zachariah. [c. 2008-2009]. Sociolinguistic survey of the 'Maya' peoples (Bali, Kpasham, Yoti) of Adamawa State. SIL Nigeria (unpublished survey report underlying Blench's wordlist compilation).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Survey reports sometimes include a phonology note; would also fix the dialect identity of the Bali wordlist. Existence inferred from Blench's introduction; never seen listed on sil.

sources.citation: A Guide prepared at the Maya orthography workshop. 2007. Bali (Adamawa State): Maya Language Development Board.

sources.note: The only other source on Maya/Bali known to Zheltov; orthography guides for Nigerian Adamawa languages usually contain a tone/syllable section and could contain a remark on stress.

sources.citation: Meek, C. K. 1931. Tribal Studies in Northern Nigeria, vol. I. London: Kegan Paul. (Bali and Kpasham wordlists)

sources.note: Oldest primary record of Bali; wordlist only, very unlikely to say anything about stress, listed for completeness.

sources.citation: Lyakhovich, A. V. 2012. Imennaja predikacija v jazyke vakka. In Vydrin & Zheltov (eds.), Mezhdu Nigerom i Kongo: zametki na poljah, 153-160. SPb: Nestor-Istorija. (= Glottolog ref 588337 'Elementy morfosintaksisa Jazyka Bakka', attached to bali1245)
